scenario: A 68-year-old woman has back pain, a calcium of 11.8 mg/dL, a creatinine of 2.2 mg/dL, and a hemoglobin of 9 g/dL. Her smear shows stacked red cells. She has no fever. A classmate calls it ordinary osteoporosis because the back hurts.
question: Which clone fits the four findings, and why do the red cells stack?
options: Osteoporosis, which raises calcium and stacks red cells
A plasma-cell clone. Protein coats the red cells
A chronic infection, so fever should lead and calcium falls
Iron deficiency, so the cells should be small and pale
A parathyroid adenoma, so the smear should be normal
correctAnswer: A plasma-cell clone. Protein coats the red cells
citation: Kumar V, Abbas AK, Aster JC. Robbins and Cotran Pathologic Basis of Disease. 10th ed. Elsevier; 2021.
examTakeaway: Multiple myeloma is a plasma-cell clone that punches bone, makes light chains, and stacks red cells into rouleaux.
